yes_case.case: The closest past episodes are the rollout of the Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of (Hybrid &) Electric Vehicles (FAME I in 2015 and FAME II in 2019) and the Electric Mobility Promotion Scheme (EMPS 2024). This episode differs fundamentally by shifting away from broad, fragmented consumer demand subsidies toward targeted, heavy-duty supply-side and financial architecture—specifically credit guarantees and interest subsidies tailored exclusively for commercial e-buses and e-trucks. Unlike the bureaucratic delays that plagued the transition between FAME II and PM E-Drive, this upcoming scheme is preceded by intense industry consultations and a specific mandate for heavy commercial vehicles, narrowing the policy design phase and making it distinctively more focused on institutional financing derisking rather than direct-to-consumer retail discounts.

yes_case.deliberately_ignored: Budgetary allocation amounts, bureaucratic procedural steps, inter-ministerial sign-off schedules, and exact calendar dates of cabinet approvals.

no_case.case: The two closest past episodes are the rollout of the FAME-II (Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of Hybrid and Electric Vehicles) scheme modifications in mid-2021 and the launch of the PM e-Drive Scheme in late 2024. In both of those historical precedents, heavy commercial vehicles (e-buses and specifically e-trucks) were either heavily sidelined, restricted to urban public transit pilot allocations, or had their dedicated financial components deferred due to intense inter-ministerial friction between the Ministry of Heavy Industries and the Ministry of Finance regarding capital outlays, interest subvention mechanics, and credit guarantee defaults. This episode differs fundamentally because the proposed scope attempts to target private commercial freight via direct credit guarantees—a mechanism the Ministry of Finance has historically resisted backing for heavy commercial segments due to contingent liability fears. Unlike the FAME transitions, which built upon pre-existing subsidy architectures, a standalone dedicated financing scheme for e-trucks requires novel risk-sharing frameworks with public sector banks that have repeatedly stalled in inter-ministerial working groups during past green-finance initiatives.
key_evidence: FAME-II scheme modifications in 2021 which deferred dedicated heavy commercial truck incentives
PM e-Drive Scheme launch in late 2024 which prioritized two-wheelers and public buses over private e-truck credit guarantees
Historical resistance from the Ministry of Finance to underwrite direct credit guarantee defaults for heavy commercial vehicle manufacturing

no_case.deliberately_ignored: The exact calendar timelines, administrative approval stages, cabinet committee voting schedules, bureaucrat movement, and numerical calculations of EV adoption rates across Indian states.
